title: Opinion: The Amazonian trap | Institute for Family Studies
gist: This is a short IFS 'In The News' stub, not a full article: it carries only the opening two paragraphs of a Maria Baer and Brad Wilcox opinion piece published in Deseret News on 19 July 2026 before cutting off at 'Continues...'. The excerpt sets up the Amazon myth — warrior women who kept no husbands, raised only daughters and cauterized their breasts — as the archetype of a recurring fantasy that a woman becomes strongest by providing for and protecting herself rather than pairing with a man.

themes.theme: The Amazon myth as cultural archetype

insights.claim: The Amazons of Greek mythology are presented as a civilization built on the single premise that women could build a world of their own without men — keeping no husbands, raising only daughters and sending their sons away.
insights.speaker: Maria Baer and Brad Wilcox
insights.so_what: Establishes the rhetorical frame that family-focused commentators are now using to characterise female-independence culture — expect the label to recur in this debate.
insights.quote: Legend has it that the Amazons, the warrior women of Greek mythology, built a civilization on a single premise: Women could build a world of their own without men.
insights.locator: Legend has it that the Amazons

insights.claim: The authors argue the Amazon legend reflects a fantasy that has recurred across different times, places and peoples: that a woman becomes strongest not by pairing with a man but by providing for and protecting herself, often supported by strong female peers.
insights.speaker: Maria Baer and Brad Wilcox
insights.so_what: The authors treat contemporary female self-sufficiency as a recurring cultural pattern rather than a modern novelty, which is how they justify treating it as a durable trend.
insights.quote: that a woman becomes strongest not by pairing with a man but by providing for and protecting herself — often with the support of some strong sisters

insights.claim: The Institute for Family Studies runs an 'In The News' channel that republishes only the opening paragraphs of its fellows' mainstream-outlet op-eds before cutting to 'Continues...', in this case a Maria Baer and Brad Wilcox piece in Deseret News dated 19 July 2026.
insights.speaker: Maria Baer and Brad Wilcox
insights.so_what: Shows IFS operating as a placement shop into mainstream op-ed pages rather than only publishing in-house — the distribution mechanism behind the pronatalist narrative's reach.
insights.quote: Maria Baer, Brad Wilcox, Deseret News, July 19, 2026

insights.claim: The same stub page lists Brad Wilcox appearing across The Washington Post, The Isabel Brown Show and the Java with Juli podcast within a single week in July 2026, showing a single researcher saturating outlets from legacy print to niche podcasts.
insights.speaker: Maria Baer and Brad Wilcox
insights.so_what: Illustrates how a small think tank achieves outsized narrative share through one high-frequency spokesperson across ideologically varied channels.
